title: Hosted API slab-tier COGS forecast
sheets:
Summary

Purpose, at a glance:
- Build a slab + tiered COGS model to evaluate: reserved capacity tiers, burst margins, slab discounts for committed tokens, and regional uplift modifiers.
- Produce quick decision knobs for pricing/product to test a two-month pilot offering tiered commit slabs for high-volume customers.

Key outputs (this sheet):
- Estimated per-token COGS by model and region under 3 slab scenarios
- Break-even token price for each slab given target margin
- Sensitivity to average sequence length and cache hit-rate

Primary assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline model families: small-chat (7B), medium-chat (13B), large-chat (70B)
- Baseline GPU amortization: $2,400 / GPU-month (inclusive infra) -> amortized per-token depends on throughput profile
- Average token lengths: prompt 60, completion 120 for baseline workload
- Cache hit-rate baseline: 18% (prefix/KV reuse)
- Network + infra overhead per token: $0.0000025 baseline (varies by region)

Quick conclusions (recommendations draft):
1) Offer 3 slabs (Bronze: 0-100M tokens/mo, Silver: 100M-500M, Gold: 500M+). Use progressively steeper slab discounts but require 3mo commit at Silver/Gold.
2) For US-west/EU regions, price floor can go ~12-18% below current list if we accept reserved capacity with 60% utilization; for APAC add 6-9% uplift to cover power/instance premiums.
3) Introduce a burst buffer at 15% of peak capacity billed at list price to avoid SLA degradation.

Open questions:
- How to map model-mix changes inside a customer (e.g., 13B -> 70B swing) into slab overrun triggers?
- Can we pilot Gold slab with 6 customers first to validate utilization assumptions?

Notes:
- GPU-days-per-100M calculated from baseline throughput and amortization; compute-cost uses $2,400/GPU-month baseline and instance utilization assumptions.
- Per-token-cogs here excludes variable support/ops overhead (add ~5% for supportable customers).

Slab-Tiers-Scenarios

Columns: Slab, Monthly-token-range, Slab-discount, Required-commit-length, Expected-utilization, Effective-per-token-cogs-USW, Effective-per-token-cogs-EU, Effective-per-token-cogs-APAC, Break-even-price@20pct-margin-USW
Bronze, 0 - 100,000,000, 0%, 0mo, 35%, [calc], [calc], [calc], [calc]
Silver, 100,000,001 - 500,000,000, 8%, 3mo, 55%, [calc], [calc], [calc], [calc]
Gold, 500,000,001+, 18%, 6mo, 75%, [calc], [calc], [calc], [calc]

Scenario A - conservative: assume sequence length up +25%, cache hit-rate -5pp. Impact: GPU-days +18% on avg, Slab effective cost increases ~12-14% in USW.
Scenario B - optimistic: sequence length -10%, cache hit-rate +8pp. Impact: GPU-days -9%, Slab effective cost decreases ~7-9% in EU/APAC.

Worked example (Silver, US-WEST, model-mix = 40% 7B / 40% 13B / 20% 70B):
- Weighted per-token baseline USW = 0.4*0.0000205 + 0.4*0.0000285 + 0.2*0.0001295 = $0.00004594
- Utilization uplift target -> at 55% utilization compute amortized drop to effective per-token = $0.0000358
- Apply 8% slab discount -> customer price floor = $0.0000329
- Break-even at 20% margin = $0.0000411 (list price recommendation > this)

Operational notes for pilot:
- Instrument slab customers with token telemetry and model tags to detect model-mix shifts monthly.
- Add a monthly "overage reconciliation" that invoices overrun tokens at list price and credits on next month if commitment renewed.
- Track three pilot customers (A,B,C) with expected combined commit = 1.2B tokens/mo and initial expected utilization 62%. Monitor weekly for two months.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: customers push heavier model mix -> Mitigation: auto-fallback quotas per-customer and clear overage triggers
- Risk: regional power spikes -> Mitigation: geo-fallback routing + dynamic per-region uplift applied to slab pricing
notes: Working draft for product + finance. Do not share externally. Next steps: sync with pricing legal (Jan contract template), ops to validate instrumentation plan (Opt-2184). Requesting finance run hourly-sensitivity sim (Monte Carlo) on utilization assumptions before pilot sign-ups.
